S, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE S VISHWAJITH SHETTY  ORAL ORDER 1. Accused in Special Case No.51/2024 pending before the Court of Addl.

District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-I, Davanagere, arising out of Crime No.48/2024 registered by Santhebennur Police Station, Davanagere, for the offences punishable under Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Section 376(2)(n) of IPC, is before this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. seeking regular bail.

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned HCGP for respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2, who is served in the matter has remained unrepresented before this Court.

3. FIR in Crime No.48/2024 was registered by Santhebennur Police Station, Davanagere, for the aforesaid offences against the petitioner herein on the basis of the first information dated 11.03.2024 received from respondent No.2, who is the mother of the victim girl.
During the course of investigation of the case, NC: 2024:KHC:45499 petitioner herein was arrested on 12.03.2024 and remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed against him for the aforesaid offences.
Bail application filed by petitioner before the jurisdictional Sessions Court in Special Case No.51/2024 was rejected on 05.08.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner and the victim girl were in love.
A false allegation has been made after relationship between the parties had failed.
Petitioner, who is a youngster is in custody from 12.03.2024.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition.
He submits that victim has made serious allegations in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., and the DNA report also supports the charge sheet allegations made against the petitioner.

Accordingly, he prays to dismiss Annappa vs State Of Karnataka on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23968482/
2 the petition.
6. First information was submitted by respondent No.2, who is the mother of the minor victim girl after the victim girl was NC: 2024:KHC:45499 found to be pregnant.
On 10.03.2024, victim girl was found vomiting in her house and therefore, the first informant and her husband had taken her to the Hospital for treatment.

The doctor at SS Hospital, Davanagere after medically examining the victim girl informed the first informant that victim girl was pregnant and on enquiry, the victim girl allegedly had mentioned that petitioner was the cause for her pregnancy.
It is under these circumstances, FIR has been registered against the petitioner.
Subsequently, the victim girl was subjected to medical examination and her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., was also recorded before the jurisdictional Magistrate on 26.03.2024.
The victim girl has made allegation against the petitioner about he having sexual intercourse with her against her wishes.
In her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., she has also stated that after the petitioner learnt that she was pregnant, he had informed her that he intended to marry some other girl.

The DNA test report obtained in the present case supports the allegations made against the petitioner in the charge sheet and he is found to be the biological father of the dead baby born to the victim girl.
Petitioner hails from the very same village where the victim and NC: 2024:KHC:45499 her parents are residing.
In her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., victim girl has stated that petitioner had threatened her.

Considering the aforesaid aspects of the matter and the gravity of offences committed by the petitioner, I am of the opinion that his prayer for grant of regular bail cannot be entertained at this stage.
Accordingly, petition is dismissed.

Sd/-
